lesson.grammar_point: review: choosing the right tense (Block 1 checkpoint)

vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: To continue with something even when it gets hard or slow
To reach a place or a situation you did not plan
To manage with the little money or help you have
To slowly start to feel at home in a new place
Regular and unhurried, without sudden changes
To stop and think carefully about where you are now
A chance to begin again, leaving the old life behind

vocab.text: Notice the pair: you settle IN to a place, but you stick WITH a task. The preposition carries the meaning.

paras: Marina Alcantara grew up in a crowded apartment ten minutes from downtown Sao Paulo. In 2015, when she was thirty-eight, she left the city and ended up in a town of eleven thousand people. She visited it only once before she moved. Her friends said she would be bored within a year, and while they were saying that, she was already packing her belongings. On the whole, they were wrong.

The first months were hard. The town is much quieter than the city and life there is far cheaper, but there is a lot less to do. It took her almost two years to settle in. What saved her, she says, was the house: a worn-out farmhouse from the nineteen fifties that nobody else wanted. The roof was replaced in the first winter and the old wiring was redone by an electrician. The floors were stripped and sanded down by hand, by her. Right now the kitchen is being rebuilt.

Marina has been working on that house for nine years. She has never hired a designer and she has never followed a plan. Progress is slow but steady: one room a year, sometimes less. Three stray dogs have ended up living there too. She gets by on far less money than she earned in the city, and she says the house gave her something the city never did: a sense of purpose. "I take stock every January," she says. "I look at what was finished, and then I stick with the next thing. In the evening I unwind on the porch with the dogs and I look forward to the quiet. It was exhausting, and on the whole it was the best decision I have ever made."

reading.prompt: What is the best title for this text?
choices: How to buy a cheap house in the countryside
Nine years, one house, and a different life
Why small towns are losing their young people

items: Marina moved to the town without ever seeing it.
The text says she visited it once, before she moved.
It took Marina about two years to feel at home in the town.
The text says: "It took her almost two years to settle in."
Marina hired a designer to plan the work on the house.
The text says she has never hired a designer and has never followed a plan.
Marina lives on less money now than she earned in the city.
The text says she gets by on far less money than she earned in the city.

items.situation: A new neighbor asks why you left the capital. Answer in three sentences: when you left, why, and how you feel about it now.
tips: I left Sao Paulo in ... , and I ended up here.
On the whole, it was the right decision.

items.situation: Someone asks how long you have been restoring furniture. Give the length of time, not the date.
tips: I have been doing it for about six years.
I have been at it since I moved here.

items.situation: A friend asks what was already repaired when you bought the house. Do not name who did the work.
tips: The roof was replaced before we moved in.
The wiring was redone by an electrician.

items.situation: Compare your life here with your life in the city, in two sentences.
tips: It is much quieter here than in Sao Paulo.
There is a lot less to do, but I get by on far less money.

answerkey.title: Reveal the Block 1 toolkit
list: Present simple and continuous: who you are, and what is going on right now. "I live here." / "The kitchen is being rebuilt."
Past simple and past continuous: the finished moment, and the background around it. "She left in 2015, while her friends were saying she would be bored."
Comparatives and superlatives: two places side by side. "The town is much quieter than the city."
Present perfect for experience, with no time given: "She has never hired a designer."
Present perfect continuous for how long: "She has been working on that house for nine years."
Passive voice, when the thing matters more than the person: "The roof was replaced." / "The kitchen is being rebuilt."
Expressions: to settle in, a fresh start, to end up, to take stock, to stick with, steady, to unwind, to get by, sense of purpose, to look forward to, worn out, on the whole.
answerkey.note: This is everything from Lessons 1 to 7 in one place. Block 2 is built on top of it.

listenings.text: People keep asking me whether I regret it, and the honest answer is no, not for a single day. I took stock last January, the way I always do. Nine years ago I did not know what I wanted. I was worn out, I was working every weekend, and I was getting by, but nothing more than that. Now the mornings belong to me. The work on the house is slow, but it is steady, and every room that is finished belongs to me in a way that nothing in the city ever did. I do not have a plan for next year. I have a list, and I stick with it, one line at a time. On the whole, I sleep better.

Everyone talks about the fresh start. Nobody warns you about the first winter. I moved out here in March, and by August I was seriously thinking about going back. The house was cold, the internet was terrible, and I did not know a single person in the town. It took me three years to settle in, not one. What changed things was the workshop. I started fixing chairs for the neighbors, badly at first, and I stuck with it. Now I have more work than I can handle, and I unwind in the evening by doing exactly the thing I do all day. My advice for anyone planning the same move is simple: give it three years, not one.

extra_audio.text: First, Tom asks Ana whether the move was the right decision. Then Ana says that on the whole it was, although it took her a long time to settle in. Next, Tom tells her that he sold the workshop and moved back to Sao Paulo. After that, Tom explains that he was worn out and only getting by. Finally, Ana says that it was worth it, because his son lives ten minutes away.
